Compare local-projection and VAR impulse responses

Source: R/lp-forecast.R
compare_lp_var.Rd

Plagborg-Moller & Wolf (2021): with the same lag length and the same recursive identification, population LP and VAR responses coincide at all horizons; in finite samples they differ only by estimation error. This helper estimates the LP \(y_{t+h}=\alpha_h+\beta_hy_{j,t}+\gamma_h'w_t+e\) with controls the contemporaneous variables ordered before the shock \(j\) and \(p\) lags of all variables, and the VAR(\(p\)) Cholesky response (ordering = column order) normalised to a unit impact on the shock variable, \(\Theta_h e_j/\Theta_0^{jj}\), and returns both with their difference.

Usage

compare_lp_var(
  Y,
  shock,
  horizon = 20L,
  lags = 4L,
  se = c("nw", "hc"),
  nw_lag = NULL
)

Arguments

Y

data frame / tibble / matrix (T x K) of responses (and the source of lag controls). Non-numeric columns (e.g. a date) are dropped.

shock

<tidy-select> the shock variable of Y.

horizon

maximum horizon H.

lags

number of lags of Y in the controls (and of an external shock).

se

"nw" Newey-West/Bartlett or "hc" Eicker-Huber-White (HC1).

nw_lag

Newey-West truncation lag; default h + 1.

Value

a lp_var_cmp tibble with horizon, response, lp, lp_se, var, diff = lp - var, z = diff / lp_se.

Details

Economic intuition. Choosing between LP and VAR is a bias-variance trade-off: the VAR extrapolates the first \(p\) lags to all horizons (low variance, bias if the lag order is too short for long-run dynamics), LP is unbiased for any \(h\) but has variance growing with \(h\). A divergence at long horizons that is large relative to lp_se signals VAR misspecification (or LP noise); agreement supports either. Pitfall: the comparison is only meaningful with identical lags and ordering, which this function enforces. VAR responses are point estimates (no bands).

References

Plagborg-Moller, M. and Wolf, C. (2021) Local projections and VARs estimate the same impulse responses. Econometrica.

See also

Other local projections: autoplot.lpm(), lp(), lp_forecast(), lp_joint(), lp_panel(), lp_smooth(), lp_state(), lp_supt(), tidy.lpm()

Examples

compare_lp_var(yraw, shock = unemp, horizon = 12, lags = 2)
#> <lp_var_cmp> shock 'unemp', 2 lags; mean |LP - VAR| / se_LP by horizon block:
#>         infl  rate unemp
#> short  0.274 0.276 0.701
#> medium 0.498 0.152 0.344
#> long   0.189 0.519 0.500
